recipes.name: Macaroni Salad with Pickles
ingredients_raw: 0.25 teaspoon ground black pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Cook macaroni pasta in a large pot of boiling water until al dente. Drain, rinse with cold water, and set aside.

Meanwhile, place eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water by 1 inch. Bring to a boil. Cover, remove from heat, and let stand for 20 minutes. Transfer eggs to an ice water bath. Peel and chop when cool enough to handle.
Whisk mayonnaise, sour cream, mustard, sweet pickle juice, and celery seed together in a medium bowl. Season with salt and black pepper.
Combine macaroni, celery, onion, olives, sweet pickles, carrots, green bell pepper, and eggs in a large bowl. Stir in dressing until evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate until chilled before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Macaroni Salad with Pickles
raw_recipe.description: You can double or triple this recipe and make enough for a crowd of hungry friends. The creamy mayonnaise dressing has sour cream, sweet pickle juice and mustard stirred in.

review.reviewBody: I made this for a cover dish dinner, and it did NOT last. Everyone remarked about the flavor and how creamy it was. It is so good. I did change just a couple of things. One, I left out the onion as neither my husband or myself can eat them..and it was n't missed. Also, instead of using pickle juice and the sweet pickle, I used sweet relish. I did increase the dressing half again, as we do not like a dry macaroni salad, and this did not get dry. I made it the day before, and yes, it tastes better the second day after the ingredients have had a chance to sit and blend. I put the carrots through my food processor and they were perfect for this salad. And one little tip. When using celery seed, rub the seeds between your palms to crush them a little. This releases not only the aroma, but the flavor as well. Oh, and if you are making a dish that requires both onion and celery, cut the celery last, and rub some leaves, or even part of the rib on your hands. It will remove the onion.
Boiled eggs with pasta to save time. Missing ground mustard so had to use a couple teaspoons of prepared mustard. Added some fresh chopped tomato for color. Very, very good. Thank you for the recipe.
Kinda bland but added more pickles and brine; can’t eat green peppers. Added English mustard too and garlic salt.Had to use dill pickles as didn’t have gherkins. Made lots and shared with neighbors.

The first time I made it I followed the recipe exactly as written and thought the celery seed was overpowering. I have made it many times since and have either omitted the celery seed or used just a teaspoon and love it.

5.30.16 Holy smokes does this make a lot of macaroni salad, enough to feed an army! IMO this will give you ten servings, at least (and I’m not talking tiny servings, either) rather than six. I liked many things about this salad. The sweetness of the chopped pickles and juice contrasted nicely with the saltiness of the olives. I also liked the dry ground mustard (I used Coleman’s®) instead of regular mustard in the dressing, gave it a little tang. Changed just a couple things...I used Miracle Whip instead of mayo (family preference for mac salad), and I cut back on the celery seed, since I thought that amount might be overwhelming. Linda, nice recipe!

I made it and it’s perfect! I was looking for a side salad for company and this had just what I thought I might like. I’ve cooked for 50 years and could never find just what I wanted. I added pepperoni minis (1 cup) and a handful of mild shredded cheddar cheese just because I had it. Even more perfect! Or just exactly this recipe. Either one!
Recipe is pretty good, but calls for way more celery seed than is needed. I believe two teaspoons would be more reasonable. Makes a lot of macaroni salad!

In refridgerator cooling now. Haven't tasted yet but just wanted to say (for those complaining about being TOO dry) I used 16oz, uncooked Macaroni with Miracle Whip (1 cup) & (1/2 cup) Sour Cream, It's plenty moist & creamy for my tastes as I don't like "soupy" Mac. salads. Left out olives & will update when I eat some.

I adjusted the servings on the recipe to 4, and the amount of pasta was still too much. So, I used all ingredients on the adjusted 4 serving recipe, but I reduced the pasta to just 1 cup dry. That worked, and the result was great!
This was delicious!....but the tip from the review to add a Tbsp. of real lemon and a Tbsp. of honey really added a sixth star!
This a really nice recipe. I used different colored peppers of added color and subbed in a bit of Greek yogurt to help cut down some of the fat. This is a keeper!
Loved this! My family loved it, too.
I liked it and loved the pickles
I did my own spin on this macaroni, salad recipe and added bacon. It’s tasty a little paprika Yum Yum.

I used dill pickles and dill pickle juice but kept the recipe the same otherwise, and it was pretty good. I'm not a huge fan of onions so I diced them super small and I think next time I will leave it out completely.
it was nice

Big hit at last two BBQ's I attended. Takes a while to make but is worth it. I buy pre-cooked eggs & use shredded carrots. I put the olives on the side b/c I'm not a fan. I also use a San Giorgio Tri Italiano pasta instead of elbows and guests were a fan of that.
I have made this recipe several times now and it is the most requested macaroni salad I have ever made! Everyone loves it!
Made some personal tweak's, things I don't eat were omitted but this is the best pasta salad I have every had.
Wow! The pickle juice and pimento stuffed green olives really jazzes up this recipe. This was a hit at our Memorial Day celebration!
